Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 59
  gender: Female
  ethnicity: Latin American
  relationship_status: Divorced
  occupation: Project Manager
  trauma_type: Captivity
  pcl5: 77

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Entrapment: Having no options, Locked Spaces: Being in a locked or confined room, Somatic Pain (Neck): Neck pain
  Maladaptive Strategies: Magical Thinking: I tell myself the event did not really happen or was not that bad, Self-Blame Rumination: I dwell on what I have done wrong, Overanalysing: I go over and over the details of the event trying to make sense of it
  Threat: Alert at Home: I feel on guard even inside my own home, Cannot Relax: I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place, False Alarms: I often react as if I am in danger even when nothing is actually wrong
  Negative Appraisals: Lost Happiness: I used to be a happy person but now I am always miserable., Emotional Numbness: I feel dead inside, Fear of Harm: You can never know who will harm you

Vignette:
Sofia Hernandez still remembers the day she was held captive by her ex-husband. It had been a bitter divorce, with months of escalating threats and intimidation. But nothing could have prepared her for the night he showed up at her doorstep, drunk and enraged, refusing to leave until she signed over the deeds to their jointly owned business. The hours that followed were a blur of fear and desperation as Sofia tried to reason with him, her mind racing with escape plans that seemed increasingly impossible. The memory of being trapped in her own home, with no way out, still haunts Sofia. Even now, years later, she finds herself avoiding small, enclosed spaces - elevators, cramped meeting rooms, even her own pantry. The feeling of claustrophobia is overwhelming, making it hard for her to breathe and think clearly. Her solution has been to plan her days meticulously, always scouting out escape routes and exit strategies before entering any new space. Sofia's body also carries the scars of that night - a persistent neck pain that seems to throb with anxiety whenever she feels trapped or confined. She has tried physical therapy and medication, but nothing seems to ease the ache completely. As a project manager, Sofia is used to being in control, but this lingering pain has made her feel vulnerable and helpless. In an effort to cope with these feelings of powerlessness, Sofia often finds herself resorting to magical thinking - telling herself that the whole ordeal was just a bad dream, or that she somehow brought it on herself by not being strong enough. She knows intellectually that this isn't true, but the narrative has become a comforting habit nonetheless. Alongside this self-justification, Sofia also dwells on what she could have done differently - replaying every conversation and encounter with her ex-husband in an attempt to make sense of it all. As a result, Sofia's daily life is now marked by hypervigilance and anxiety. She feels constantly "on guard" even inside her own home, as if danger might be lurking around the corner. Even when she knows intellectually that she is safe, her body refuses to relax - making it hard for her to fall asleep or enjoy quiet moments of solitude. The smallest creaks and groans of the house can set off alarm bells in her mind, sending her heart racing with fear. Sofia has come to believe that happiness is a luxury she can no longer afford. She used to be an optimistic person, but now every waking moment feels tinged with sadness and dread. Her friends and family have noticed the change too - commenting on how withdrawn and distant Sofia seems, as if she's lost touch with her own emotions. In truth, Sofia feels "dead inside" - like she's just going through the motions of life without any genuine feeling or purpose. As a result, Sofia has started to withdraw from social interactions altogether - afraid of being hurt again by someone she trusts. She is certain that no one can be truly trusted - that anyone could turn on her at a moment's notice. Even her own children have noticed her increased wariness around them - as if she's waiting for the other shoe to drop. It was only when Sofia realized that this fear had started to impact her relationships with loved ones, and even her job performance, that she knew she needed help. The anxiety had become too much to manage on her own, and she found herself wondering if she would ever be able to break free from the cycle of fear and mistrust.
